label: PF Backlog 633
title: [Gate 2.5] architect_review decodes git diff with the OS locale: UnicodeDecodeError on Windows + divergent review sha
body: architect_review._git_diff()/changed_files()/_merge_base() call subprocess.run(..., text=True), which decodes with the OS locale. On Windows (cp1252) any diff containing non-cp1252 bytes (em dashes, arrows, non-breaking hyphens in docs) raises UnicodeDecodeError, so the Gate 2.5 review/gate cannot run locally; and where it does decode, the sha can differ from Linux CI, forcing duplicate '<item>-<ci-sha>.json' evidence files (see BI-PF-1432/BI-PF-1395). Fix: force UTF-8 decoding in one git helper.

delivery.note: Shared UTF-8/fail-closed git helper (scripts/dev/gitutil.py); Gate 2.5 sha now locale-independent, CI reused the local evidence sha.

objective: Make Gate 2.5 git diff decoding locale-independent (UTF-8) so local Windows and Linux CI compute the same sha without crashing.
acceptance_criteria: architect_review runs every git subprocess through a helper that decodes stdout as UTF-8 (errors=replace) instead of the OS locale, so a diff containing non-cp1252 characters (e.g. em dashes) no longer raises UnicodeDecodeError on Windows.
A regression test asserts the git helper forces encoding='utf-8' with errors='replace' (and not text=True), and that non-ASCII diff text is returned decoded rather than crashing.

The Python decode path is locale-independent: a real git diff containing non-cp1252 UTF-8 decodes correctly and the gate accepts evidence for one sha; remaining git-config/attribute normalization is out of scope for this item.

summary: Gate 2.5 tool crashes or diverges across OSes because git stdout is decoded with the locale instead of UTF-8.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Add a single `_git_output(args) -> str` helper in architect_review that runs subprocess with encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', text=False and decodes bytes explicitly; route _git_diff/changed_files/_merge_base through it. Mirror the pattern used in core/github.py where a UTF-8-safe git run already exists.
dependency_findings: BI-PF-1432/1435 related: sha-duplicate evidence files depend on deterministic decoding
BI-PF-1428 related: Gate 2.5 hard-rule enforcement depends on this running on Windows
conflict_findings: No concurrent item currently modifies architect_review; risk only if BI-PF-1428 lands simultaneously
duplication_findings: BI-PF-0257 fixed cp1252 in backlog CLI console — same class of bug, do not regress
Verify core/github.py and merge_gate.py do not already ship a UTF-8 git wrapper to reuse verbatim
analysis.rationale: Small, isolated MODIFY of one helper; forces UTF-8 decoding, removes platform-dependent sha drift and unblocks local Gate 2.5 on Windows.
assumptions: UTF-8 is already the repo-wide encoding on Linux CI
Git outputs UTF-8 for these repos by default
risks: errors='replace' could mask genuine binary diffs in evidence hashes
Windows CI coverage may be absent, so fix could regress unobserved
missing_info: Whether CI runs any Windows runner that could validate the fix
Whether errors='replace' or errors='strict' is preferred for evidence fidelity

api_impact.reason: Developer tooling only (scripts/dev/architect_review.py); no runtime API surface.

2.note: Fail-closed is intended; CI uses fetch-depth 0 so origin/develop resolves. Fresh/shallow clones must fetch the integration branch first.

3.note: architect_review always uses origin/develop (present in CI and after fetch); precheck also supports a local develop because it runs from worktrees. A shared resolver is a follow-up, not required here.

4.note: False positive: subprocess is imported at module scope in architect_review_check.py (line 19).

5.note: Test sys.path mirrors existing repo test conventions; a conftest refactor is separate.

6.note: errors=replace is deterministic and warned; true byte-loss is rare and preferable to a crash.

7.note: gate1_check reads stored evidence and does not compute a diff; CLI callers fail loudly (fail-closed).

8.note: git_text accepts a per-call timeout; 30s is the inherited default.

9.note: Simple stderr warning; structured logging is out of scope.

10.note: _DEV_DIR insertion mirrors the dev-script convention already used by precheck/architect_review.
